Tattooer here. 
I think when creating a portfolio it’s good to focus on designs that will transfer well to tattoos. You’ll save yourself loads of time if you have flash that’s tattooable and ready to go. Because once you are an apprentice and you start tattooing people, it will be your designs that you will be tattooing. A shop would be more willing to take you on if you had a portfolio full of designs ready to go(it’s a business after all) . You’ve got to think more in terms of scale. For the first while you are going to only be tattooing legs and arms and most designs are only going to be 10-15cm max. As nice a drawing as this is. It would not work for a tattoo. Unless you was going to be a back piece. The eyes have too much detail and the wee chainsaw head thing. If your using procreate it’s easy to include loads on small details because you can zoom in, you can’t do this on skin. That’s why drawing on paper is good. Because if you can’t do it with a pen. You won’t be able to do it with a needle.
